# Presentation

`cinnabar:extension/presentation@0.1.0`

Mod-supplied parameters of native world presentation; requires hud authority, and nonempty
per-actor lists also players or entities. Each call replaces this mod's retained value once
the callback succeeds; a callback may make 8 presentation calls, and one more traps it.
Limits are the constants in `mod_api::presentation`.

The client merges loaded mods in load order. The earliest mod that sets a nametag style, a
hurt overlay or chat actions owns that policy. For each runtime ID and surface, the earliest
mod whose grants admit the actor's kind owns the row: players need the players grant, other
actors the entities grant, and rows a mod's grants do not admit never apply. Tooltip lines
append in load order.

**Grants:** `hud`; actor rows additionally require `players` or `entities` for their kind.

Imported type `rgba`: [`rgba`](render.md#type-rgba).

## Types

<a id="type-nametag-style"></a>

### `nametag-style`

Parameters of the native nametag renderer: opacity 0–1, scale 0.5–3, border width 0–8.
Text colours replace the native ones when present; annotation spans keep their own.

```wit
record nametag-style {
    hide: bool,
    hide-players: bool,
    hide-passengers: bool,
    show-self: bool,
    show-when-hud-hidden: bool,
    opacity: f32,
    scale: f32,
    shadow: bool,
    border-width: f32,
    text-color: option<rgba>,
    own-text-color: option<rgba>,
    border-color: option<rgba>,
    background-color: option<rgba>,
}
```

| `hide-players` | `bool` |  |

<a id="type-annotation-position"></a>

### `annotation-position`

Where annotation spans go relative to the native name. Spans draw end to end in list
order, with nothing inserted between them. `before` and `after` extend the name's first
line, and the host inserts exactly one space between the name and the spans; any other
separator belongs in the spans. `above` and `below` draw the spans on their own centred
line above the name's first line or below its last. A player-list row has one line, so
roster spans placed `above` or `below` follow the name as `after` does.

```wit
enum annotation-position {
    before,
    after,
    above,
    below,
}
```

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `before` |  |  |
| `after` |  |  |
| `above` |  |  |
| `below` |  |  |

<a id="type-annotation"></a>

### `annotation`

Text attached to one actor's eligible nametag and, for a player whose actor the client
knows, that player's player-list row. Each surface holds up to `MAX_ANNOTATION_SPANS`
spans; an empty list leaves that surface native. Nametag spans on the local player also
show its own tag. Runtime IDs are nonzero and distinct within one call.

```wit
record annotation {
    runtime-id: u64,
    nametag: list<text-span>,
    nametag-position: annotation-position,
    roster: list<text-span>,
    roster-position: annotation-position,
}
```

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime-id` | `u64` |  |
| `nametag` | `list<text-span>` |  |
| `nametag-position` | `annotation-position` |  |
| `roster` | `list<text-span>` |  |
| `roster-position` | `annotation-position` |  |

Types: [`annotation-position`](presentation.md#type-annotation-position), [`text-span`](presentation.md#type-text-span).

<a id="type-tooltip-line"></a>

### `tooltip-line`

One extra item tooltip line of plain text, at most `MAX_TOOLTIP_LINE_BYTES`; metadata
none matches every variant. One item's tooltip shows at most `MAX_ITEM_TOOLTIP_LINES`.

```wit

    identifier: string,
    metadata: option<u32>,
    text: string,
    color: rgba,
}
```

Types: [`rgba`](render.md#type-rgba).

<a id="type-chat-action"></a>

### `chat-action`

A clickable span: a primary click or tap on `text` inside a message of the open chat
history closes the chat and reports `action`, with value 1, among `input.read-controls`
events on the owning mod's next frame; reading it requires controls authority. `text` is
at most `MAX_CHAT_ACTION_TEXT_BYTES`; `action` is at most `MAX_CHAT_ACTION_ID_BYTES` of
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`.

```wit
record chat-action {
    text: string,
    action: string,
}
```

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` |  |
| `action` | `string` |  |

<a id="set-hurt-overlay"></a>

### `set-hurt-overlay`

```wit
set-hurt-overlay: func(body: option<rgba>, armor: option<rgba>) -> result<_, string>;
```

Native damage overlay colours for actor bodies and their armour, while an actor is hurt;
none keeps native. One policy: the earliest mod setting either colour owns both.

Types: [`rgba`](render.md#type-rgba).
